subject: Privacy & Digital Rights
title: Surveillance and Democracy
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Surveillance and Democracy.

hook.text: Democracy requires free speech, free assembly, and a free press. Surveillance chills all three.

buildup.text: When people know they're watched, they self-censor. They avoid protests, whispers, and dissent.

discovery.text: Studies show that internet surveillance measurably reduces online searches for sensitive political topics.

twist.text: Authoritarian regimes use surveillance openly. Democracies do it quietly — but the effect is similar.

climax.text: A democracy that watches its citizens too closely stops being a democracy. It just keeps the name.

punchline.text: Watch everyone, silence everyone. Democracy dies quietly.

quiz.question: How does surveillance affect democratic participation?
options: It causes self-censorship and reduced political engagement
It has no measurable effect on behavior
